sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: WNT7A/WNT7B co-stimulation assay in transfected cells: N-terminal FLAG-tagged GPR124 potentiated WNT signaling equivalently to untagged GPR124 — function fully preserved.
sites.rationale: ADGRA2 and GPR124 are the same gene; L2 is therefore direct (not ortholog) evidence. The signal peptide spans residues 1–33 (computed landmarks), so an N-terminal FLAG tag must be placed after cleavage, i.e., insert_after_residue = 33. Python confirms seq[32]='G' and seq[33]='A', matching residue_before/after. No residue is named in the paper, so position_evidence is topology_derived — the mature N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus available. L3 and L4 (FLAG-tagged zebrafish Gpr124 ortholog, surface ELISA and in-vivo immunostaining confirmed) independently corroborate surface display at this same topological position. L2 reports that an N-terminal FLAG tag added to full-length human GPR124 (= ADGRA2) expressed in a cell-based WNT co-stimulation assay did not interfere with receptor activity. GPR124 carries a signal peptide (residues 1–33); the only extracellular N-terminus available to a FLAG tag is the mature N-terminus beginning at Ala34. No residue number is named in the paper, so the junction is derived from the single available extracellular terminus: after residue 33 (last SP residue, G) and before residue 34 (A).

sources.claim: Mouse GPR124 and human GPR124 also showed similar co-stimulatory activity, and addition of an N-terminal FLAG tag or a C-terminal myc tag to GPR124 did not interfere with its ability to potentiate WNT signaling ( Figures 2C and 2D ).

literature_notes: Eight ledger lines were evaluated. L2 grounds the single surface site: an N-terminal FLAG tag on full-length human GPR124/ADGRA2 with WNT function preserved; position is topology-derived (after SP cleavage, residue 33→34) because no residue number is stated. L3 and L4 (FLAG-tagged zebrafish Gpr124, surface ELISA and in-vivo immunostaining) corroborate the same topological position on the ortholog but do not add a distinct site. L1 (V5 after Arg1074, 10 aa downstream of TM7) is intracellular and placed in other_positions. L5, L6, L7 (C-terminal EGFP on zebrafish Adgra2) and L8 (C-terminal Myc on human GPR124) all tag the intracellular C-terminus (residues 1069–1338 per landmarks) and are placed in other_positions. The large extracellular domain (residues 34–771) and the three short ECLs (ECL1 827–836, ECL2 908–924, ECL3 1041–1047) have no ledger evidence for internal insertions and are not proposed as sites.

literature_other_positions.note: V5 tag + stop codon inserted after Arg1074 (10 aa downstream of TM7, within the intracellular C-terminal domain 1069–1338) to truncate the ICD and study its role in CNS angiogenesis.
Myc epitope (EQKLISEEDL) inserted at the C-terminus of human GPR124; the C-terminus (residue 1338) falls within the intracellular domain (1069–1338) per topology landmarks.

C-terminal EGFP fusion to zebrafish Adgra2 (ortholog of human ADGRA2); the C-terminus is intracellular; the tagged protein was functional in vivo but the tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
